subject: physics
question_text: Two vectors of equal magnitude have a resultant equal in magnitude to either of them. What is the angle between them?

verification.note: PREDICTED — Session 89 enumeration sweep (archetype × object grid over the NCERT chapter): this question has not appeared in any paper or source book we hold, but the chapter contains it and the 2-mark/4-mark format admits it. Authored as a lean card; promote to a full card when a paper season or a Telangana IPE teacher validates the cell. Split invented, as everywhere.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Setting up
lines: Let each vector have magnitude P and let θ
be the angle between them. The resultant
steps.margin_note: First mark. Write the parallelogram formula with P in every place.
steps.why: Writing "the resultant is also P" as an equation is the whole question; the algebra after it is two lines.
common_mistakes: Setting the resultant to 2P instead of P.

recall.must_convey: That putting R equal to P in the parallelogram formula gives P squared equals 2P squared plus 2P squared cos theta.
accept: P squared equals P squared plus P squared plus 2 P squared cos theta

steps.memory_tip: The words "equal to either of them" mean R = P, not 2P. The same P goes in all three places.

steps.label: Solving
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The angle is the answer — write 120°, not just cos θ = −½.
steps.why: A negative cosine means an obtuse angle — the two vectors point further apart, and that is what squeezes the resultant back down to P.
common_mistakes: Reading cos θ = −½ as 60° instead of 120°.

recall.must_convey: That cos theta comes out as minus half, so theta is 120 degrees.

steps.memory_tip: Check it: at 120° the two vectors and their resultant form an equilateral triangle.

insider_note: Setting up P² = P² + P² + 2P·P cos θ is a full mark on its own. Writing 120° with no setup earns one mark, not two.
